newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close lower, break support.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close lower, break support.

text.p: The Philippine stock market main index settled lower on Thursday, pushed below its support level by continued worries over the impact of the Thai financial crisis on the peso.

"There were still concerns over the volatility of the Thai baht which overshadowed the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates steady," said Mayenne Katimbang, research head at Magnum International Securities Inc.
The main index closed 22.47 points down, or 0.81 percent, at 2,742.42 points, piercing through its 2,750 support.

"The Thailand baht reached an all-time low on Wednesday so there is still that concern that what happened to Thailand's baht may happen to the rest of the region," said David de la Cruz, vice-president for marketing at Amsteel Securities.
The Central Bank strongly defended the peso from speculation on Wednesday after Thailand announced it was adopting a managed float policy for its currency.
On Thursday, all Manila stocks indices fell and in the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 70 to 34.

Banking issues led by Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co and the Philippine National Bank pushed the index down at close. Metrobank closed 20 pesos lower at 540 pesos while PNB fell three pesos to 181 pesos.
On the other hand, electronics firm Ionics Circuit Inc and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co closed higher as companies with dollar-denominated revenues were expected to post gains.
Despite the reopening of the stock market in Hong Kong, turnover was still meagre at 1.6 billion pesos.
Traders expect the market to remain tentative on Friday although concerns on foreign exchange volatility were expected to ebb.

"We still advise investors to hold on to stocks. Interest in equities will pick up as soon as we get the Thai problem out of the way which should happen in a couple of days," said Manuel Goseco, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
